claim.claim-text: 1. A method of using received signals to make location determinations, the method comprising:
2. The method of claim 1,

wherein determining whether the wireless device is in motion comprises determining that the wireless device is not in motion based on determining that the rate at which the received signal strength of beacon signals varies with time is below a received signal strength change threshold, and determining the received signal strength averaging window based on determining that the wireless device is not in motion.
3. The method of claim 1 or 2, further comprising:

wherein determining whether the wireless device is in motion comprises determining that the wireless device is in motion based on determining that the rate at which the received signal strength of beacon signals varies with time is equal to or above a received signal strength change threshold, and determining the received signal strength averaging window based on determining that the wireless device is in motion.
4. The method of claim 1, 2 or 3, further comprising: wherein determining whether the wireless device is in motion comprises at least one of:

determining that the wireless device is in a first rate of motion based on determining that the rate at which the received signal strength of beacon signals varies with time is above a first received signal strength change threshold and below a second received signal strength change threshold, or determining that the wireless device is in a second rate of motion based on determining that the rate at which the received signal strength of beacon signals varies with time is above the first received signal strength change threshold and above the second received signal strength change threshold, wherein the first rate of motion is a slower rate of motion than the second rate of motion.

5. The method of any of claims 1 to 4, wherein the received signal strength averaging window comprises a first number of time slots based on determining that the wireless device is in motion or a second number of time slots based on determining that the wireless device is not in motion, wherein the first number of time slots is less than the second number of time slots.
6. The method of any of claims 1 to 5, wherein the averaging time window is based on a velocity of the wireless device.

7. The method of any of claims 1 to 6, wherein determining whether the wireless device is in motion comprises determining that the wireless device is not in motion based on determining that the rate at which received signal strength of beacon signals from the wireless device varies with time is zero.
8. A system of using received signals to make location determinations, the system comprising: one or more processors configured to:
9. The system of claim 8,

wherein to determine whether the wireless device is in motion, the one or more processors are configured to determine that the wireless device is not in motion based on determining that the rate at which the received signal strength of beacon signals varies with time is below a received signal strength change threshold, and wherein to determine the received signal strength averaging window, the one or more processors are configured to determine the received signal strength averaging window based on determining that the wireless device is not in motion.
10. The system of claim 8 or 9, further comprising:

wherein to determine whether the wireless device is in motion, the one or more processors are configured to determine that the wireless device is in motion based on determining that the rate at which the received signal strength of beacon signals varies with time is equal to or above a received signal strength change threshold, and wherein to determine the received signal strength averaging window, the one or more processors are configured to determine the received signal strength averaging window based on determining that the wireless device is in motion.
11. The system of claim 8, 9 or 10, further comprising: wherein to determine whether the wireless device is in motion, the one or more processors are configured to perform at least one of:

determine that the wireless device is in a first rate of motion based on determining that the rate at which the received signal strength of beacon signals varies with time is above a first received signal strength change threshold and below a second received signal strength change threshold, or determine that the wireless device is in a second rate of motion based on determining that the rate at which the received signal strength of beacon signals varies with time is above the first received signal strength change threshold and above the second received signal strength change threshold, wherein the first rate of motion is a slower rate of motion than the second rate of motion.

12. The system of any of claims 8 to 11, wherein the received signal strength averaging window comprises a first number of time slots based on determining that the wireless device is in motion or a second number of time slots based on determining that the wireless device is not in motion, wherein the first number of time slots is less than the second number of time slots.
13. The system of any of claims 8-12, wherein the averaging time window is based on a velocity of the wireless device.

14. The system of claim 8, wherein to determine whether the wireless device is in motion, the one or more processors are configured to determine that the wireless device is not in motion based on determining that the rate at which received signal strength of beacon signals from the wireless device varies with time is zero.

15. A computer-readable medium encoded with instructions that, when executed by one or more programmable processors, cause the processors to become configured to perform the method recited by any of claims 1-7.
